rv.q: In "Smokey Joe's Cafe," the songs have been enshrined as theater and they can't hold up under the weight of all that attention in such a formal setting.
The music itself, even if it doesn't have much emotional range or variety, is wildly infectious, particularly the way it's sung by the sensationally talented cast.

cn.t: Critics find this Leiber and Stoller song revue breezy and bouncy, but question whether these jukebox hits translate effectively to the Broadway stage, where they struggle under the weight of theatrical presentation.
